fn prepared_registry_binding<R: CommandRunner, D: DependencyResolver>(
    workspace: &Workspace<'_, R, D>,
    target: &PublishTarget,
) -> Result<PreparedRegistryBinding, GraphError> {
    let key = target.registry_key().ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInvariant {
        detail: format!("publish target `{}` has no registry key", target.config_str()),
    })?;
    let explicit = target.registry_override();
    let configured = workspace
        .config
        .registries
        .get(&key)
        .and_then(|registry| registry.url.as_deref());
    let binding = match explicit.or(configured) {
        Some(raw) => canonical_registry_binding(key.as_str(), raw)?,
        None => {
            return Ok(PreparedRegistryBinding {
                key: key.clone(),
                endpoint: None,
                identity: RegistryBindingDigest::from_normalized_binding(key.as_str().as_bytes()),
            })
        }
    };
    Ok(PreparedRegistryBinding {
        key,
        endpoint: Some(binding.endpoint()),
        identity: binding.digest(),
    })
}

        fs::write(

            "[[package]]\nmatch = \"my-crate\"\npublish-to = [\"bogus\"]\n",

        let mut path = url.path_segments_mut().ok()?;
        path.pop_if_empty();
        path.extend(segments.iter().copied());
    }
    Some(url.to_string())
}

fn verify_github_attestation<R: CommandRunner>(
    path: &Path,
    policy: &ProvenancePolicy,
    source_commit: &callisto_model::CommitSha,
    runner: &R,
) -> Result<(), GraphError> {
    let repository_slug = policy.repository().as_slug();
    let workflow = format!("{repository_slug}/{}", policy.workflow_path());
    let path_argument = path.to_string_lossy();
    let args = [
        "attestation",
        "verify",
        path_argument.as_ref(),
        "--repo",
        repository_slug.as_str(),
        "--signer-workflow",
        workflow.as_str(),
        "--signer-digest",
        policy.workflow_commit().as_str(),
        "--source-digest",
        source_commit.as_str(),
        "--deny-self-hosted-runners",
    ];
    let output = runner
        .run_with_timeout(
            "gh",
            &args,
            path.parent().unwrap_or_else(|| Path::new(".")),
            ATTESTATION_TIMEOUT,
        )
        .map_err(|error| GraphError::ArtifactAttestation {
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            message: error.to_string(),
        })?;
    if output.success() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(GraphError::ArtifactAttestation {
            path: path.to_path_buf(),
            message: "GitHub attestation verification failed".to_owned(),
        })
    }
}

    fn observe_remote_annotated_tag(
        &self,
        remote: &str,
        name: &TagName,
        target_sha: &CommitSha,
        annotation_digest: &TagAnnotationDigest,
    ) -> Result<RemoteAnnotatedTagObservation, VcsError> {
        // Ask for both the tag object and its peeled target. `ls-remote`
        // exposes neither a tag annotation nor its object body, so after this
        // cheap absence/target check we fetch only the named tag object with
        // no local ref or FETCH_HEAD update and inspect that exact object.
        let tag_ref = format!("refs/tags/{}", name.as_str());
        let peeled_ref = format!("{tag_ref}^{{}}");
        let ls_remote = self.runner.run(
            "git",
            &["ls-remote", "--tags", "--", remote, &tag_ref, &peeled_ref],
            &self.root,
        )?;
        if !ls_remote.success() {
            return Err(remote_command_error("git ls-remote", &ls_remote));
        }
        let refs = parse_ls_remote_tag_refs(&ls_remote.stdout, &tag_ref, &peeled_ref)?;
        let Some(tag_object) = refs.tag_object else {
            return Ok(RemoteAnnotatedTagObservation::Absent);
        };
        let Some(peeled_target) = refs.peeled_target else {
            return Ok(RemoteAnnotatedTagObservation::Conflict(
                RemoteAnnotatedTagConflict::LightweightTag,
            ));
        };
        if peeled_target != *target_sha {
            return Ok(RemoteAnnotatedTagObservation::Conflict(
                RemoteAnnotatedTagConflict::Target {
                    expected: target_sha.clone(),
                    actual: peeled_target,
                },
            ));
        }

        let fetch = self.runner.run(
            "git",
            &["fetch", "--no-tags", "--no-write-fetch-head", "--", remote, &tag_ref],
            &self.root,
        )?;
        if !fetch.success() {
            return Err(remote_command_error("git fetch", &fetch));
        }
        let tag_object_id = tag_object.as_str();
        let object = self.runner.run(
            "git",
            &["--no-replace-objects", "cat-file", "-p", "--", tag_object_id],
            &self.root,
        )?;
        if !object.success() {
            return Err(remote_command_error("git cat-file", &object));
        }
        let (declared_target, actual_annotation) = parse_annotated_tag_object(&object.stdout)?;
        if declared_target != *target_sha {
            return Ok(RemoteAnnotatedTagObservation::Conflict(
                RemoteAnnotatedTagConflict::MalformedTarget,
            ));
        }
        let actual_digest = TagAnnotationDigest::from_tag_object_message(actual_annotation.as_bytes());
        if actual_digest != *annotation_digest {
            return Ok(RemoteAnnotatedTagObservation::Conflict(
                RemoteAnnotatedTagConflict::Annotation {
                    expected: annotation_digest.clone(),
                    actual: actual_digest,
                },
            ));
        }
        Ok(RemoteAnnotatedTagObservation::Exact)

pub struct ReconciledReleaseExecution {

pub fn reconcile_release_execution(
    intent: &ReleaseIntent,
    state: &ReleaseExecutionState,
) -> Result<ReconciledReleaseExecution, GraphError> {
    state
        .validate_for_intent(intent)
        .map_err(|source| GraphError::ReleaseExecutionState { source })?;
    let prerequisites: BTreeMap<_, _> = intent
        .operations()
        .iter()
        .map(|operation| (operation.id().clone(), operation.prerequisites().to_vec()))
        .collect();
    let mut eligible = Vec::new();
    for operation in intent.operations() {
        if state.operation_state(operation.id()) != Some(ReleaseOperationState::Pending) {
            continue;
        }
        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
        if prerequisites_satisfied_transitively(operation.id(), &prerequisites, state, &mut visited) {
            eligible.push(operation.id().clone());
        }
    }
    Ok(ReconciledReleaseExecution { eligible })
}

fn prerequisites_satisfied_transitively(
    id: &ReleaseOperationId,
    prerequisites: &BTreeMap<ReleaseOperationId, Vec<ReleaseOperationId>>,
    state: &ReleaseExecutionState,
    visited: &mut BTreeSet<ReleaseOperationId>,
) -> bool {
    if !visited.insert(id.clone()) {
        return false;
    }
    let result = prerequisites.get(id).is_some_and(|direct| {
        direct.iter().all(|prerequisite| {
            matches!(
                state.operation_state(prerequisite),
                Some(ReleaseOperationState::Published | ReleaseOperationState::AlreadySatisfied)
            ) && prerequisites_satisfied_transitively(prerequisite, prerequisites, state, visited)
        })
    });
    visited.remove(id);
    result
}

}

fn read_json_file(path: &std::path::Path) -> Result<serde_json::Value, CliError> {
    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|source| CliError::Io {
        source,
        path: Some(path.to_path_buf()),

    serde_json::from_str(&content)

        source,
        path: Some(path.to_path_buf()),
    })?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Builds a release intent from a fresh root-bound observation.
pub fn build_release_intent<L: ProjectLocator, R: CommandRunner>(
    root: &Path,
    locator: &L,
    runner: &R,
    decision: &ReleaseDecisionV1,
    profile_name: &str,
) -> Result<ReleaseIntent, GraphError> {
    let root = canonical_root(root)?;
    let workspace = Workspace::load(root.clone(), locator, runner)?;
    let source = observe_source(&workspace)?;
    let intent = derive_product_release(&workspace, decision, source.clone(), profile_name)?.intent;

    // Recheck after all input reads. A concurrent edit or checkout cannot be
    // authorized merely because it happened after the first check.
    if observe_source(&workspace)? != source {
        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale {
            reason: StaleReason::source_identity_changed(),
        });
    }
    Ok(intent)
}

/// Re-observes root, config, package discovery, manifests, Git evidence, and
/// the exact operation DAG before creating an opaque authorization capability.
pub fn validate_release_intent<'a, L: ProjectLocator, R: CommandRunner>(
    root: &Path,
    locator: &L,
    runner: &'a R,
    received: ReleaseIntent,
) -> Result<ValidatedReleaseIntent<'a>, GraphError> {
    validate_release_intent_with_state_directory(root, locator, runner, None, received)
}

/// Validates an intent while placing its workspace lock under an explicit
/// caller-owned state directory.
///
/// CI callers that supply an explicit durable state file must use its parent
/// here as well.  Otherwise validation would still depend on the runner's
/// implicit platform state location, defeating<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="1379" />cation-state base directory.
///
/// This is operational routing only; callers must still key state by a
/// canonical workspace and durable intent rather than treating the location
/// as release authority.
pub fn platform_state_directory() -> Result<PathBuf, VcsError> {
    #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
    {
        return Err(VcsError::Git(
            "durable release execution is unavailable on wasm32".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
    {
        #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(|home| PathBuf::from(home).join("Library/Application Support"));
        #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("LOCALAPPDATA").map(PathBuf::from);
        #[cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("XDG_STATE_HOME")
            .map(PathBuf::from)
            .or_else(|| std::env::var_os("HOME").map(|home| PathBuf::from(home).join(".local/state")));
        candidate.ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Git("could not determine platform release state directory".to_string()))
    }
}

/// Builds a release intent from a fresh root-bound observation.
pub fn build_release_intent<L: ProjectLocator, R: CommandRunner>(
    root: &Path,
    locator: &L,
    runner: &R,
    decision: &ReleaseDecisionV1,
    profile_name: &str,
) -> Result<ReleaseIntent, GraphError> {
    let root = canonical_root(root)?;
    let workspace = Workspace::load(root.clone(), locator, runner)?;
    let source = observe_source(&workspace)?;
    let intent = derive_product_release(&workspace, decision, source.clone(), profile_name)?.intent;

    // Recheck after all input reads. A concurrent edit or checkout cannot be
    // authorized merely because it happened after the first check.
    if observe_source(&workspace)? != source {
        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale {
            reason: StaleReason::source_identity_changed(),
        });
    }
    Ok(intent)
}

/// Re-observes root, config, package discovery, manifests, Git evidence, and
/// the exact operation DAG before creating an opaque authorization capability.
pub fn validate_release_intent<'a, L: ProjectLocator, R: CommandRunner>(
    root: &Path,
    locator: &L,
    runner: &'a R,
    received: ReleaseIntent,
) -> Result<ValidatedReleaseIntent<'a>, GraphError> {
    validate_release_intent_with_state_directory(root, locator, runner, None, received)
}

/// Validates an intent while placing its workspace lock under an explicit
/// caller-owned state directory.
///
/// CI callers that supply an explicit durable state file must use its parent
/// here as well.  Otherwise validation would still depend on the runner's
/// implicit platform state location, defeating<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="1379" />cation-state base directory.
///
/// This is operational routing only; callers must still key state by a
/// canonical workspace and durable intent rather than treating the location
/// as release authority.
pub fn platform_state_directory() -> Result<PathBuf, VcsError> {
    #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
    {
        return Err(VcsError::Git(
            "durable release execution is unavailable on wasm32".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
    {
        #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(|home| PathBuf::from(home).join("Library/Application Support"));
        #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("LOCALAPPDATA").map(PathBuf::from);
        #[cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("XDG_STATE_HOME")
            .map(PathBuf::from)
            .or_else(|| std::env::var_os("HOME").map(|home| PathBuf::from(home).join(".local/state")));
        candidate.ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Git("could not determine platform release state directory".to_string()))
    }
}

impl ReleaseReceiptWriter for AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter {
    fn write(&self, path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> std::io::Result<()> {

    }

/// Builds a release intent from a fresh root-bound observation.
pub fn build_release_intent<L: ProjectLocator, R: CommandRunner>(
    root: &Path,
    locator: &L,
    runner: &R,
    decision: &ReleaseDecisionV1,
    profile_name: &str,
) -> Result<ReleaseIntent, GraphError> {
    let root = canonical_root(root)?;
    let workspace = Workspace::load(root.clone(), locator, runner)?;
    let source = observe_source(&workspace)?;
    let intent = derive_product_release(&workspace, decision, source.clone(), profile_name)?.intent;

    // Recheck after all input reads. A concurrent edit or checkout cannot be
    // authorized merely because it happened after the first check.
    if observe_source(&workspace)? != source {
        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale {
            reason: StaleReason::source_identity_changed(),
        });
    }
    Ok(intent)
}

/// Validates an intent while placing its workspace lock under an explicit
/// caller-owned state directory.
///
/// CI callers that supply an explicit durable state file must use its parent
/// here as well.  Otherwise validation would still depend on the runner's
/// implicit platform state location, defeating<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="1379" />cation-state base directory.
///
/// This is operational routing only; callers must still key state by a
/// canonical workspace and durable intent rather than treating the location
/// as release authority.
pub fn platform_state_directory() -> Result<PathBuf, VcsError> {
    #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
    {
        return Err(VcsError::Git(
            "durable release execution is unavailable on wasm32".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
    {
        #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(|home| PathBuf::from(home).join("Library/Application Support"));
        #[cfg(target_os = "windows")]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("LOCALAPPDATA").map(PathBuf::from);
        #[cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))]
        let candidate = std::env::var_os("XDG_STATE_HOME")
            .map(PathBuf::from)
            .or_else(|| std::env::var_os("HOME").map(|home| PathBuf::from(home).join(".local/state")));
        candidate.ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Git("could not determine platform release state directory".to_string()))
    }
}

//! Atomic explicit-path persistence for final observation receipts.
//!
//! Receipts are output evidence, never an input authority. This store exposes
//! no load-as-proof path and accepts only a receipt that revalidates against
//! the exact intent and artifact expectations being converged.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use callisto_model::{
    atomic::atomic_write, ApplyPermit, CompleteObservationReceipt, ObservationExpectations, ReleaseIntent,
};

use crate::GraphError;

pub trait ReleaseReceiptWriter {
    fn write(&self, path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> std::io::Result<()>;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter;

impl ReleaseReceiptWriter for AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter {
    fn write(&self, path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        atomic_write(path, content, permit)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ReleaseReceiptStore<W = AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter> {
    path: PathBuf,
    writer: W,
}

impl ReleaseReceiptStore {
    pub fn new(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        Self::with_writer(path, AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter)
    }
}

impl<W: ReleaseReceiptWriter> ReleaseReceiptStore<W> {
    pub fn with_writer(path: impl Into<PathBuf>, writer: W) -> Self {
        Self {
            path: path.into(),
            writer,
        }
    }

    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.path
    }

    pub fn save(
        &self,
        intent: &ReleaseIntent,
        expectations: &ObservationExpectations,
        receipt: &CompleteObservationReceipt,

//! Atomic explicit-path persistence for final observation receipts.
//!
//! Receipts are output evidence, never an input authority. This store exposes
//! no load-as-proof path and accepts only a receipt that revalidates against
//! the exact intent and artifact expectations being converged.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use callisto_model::{
    atomic::atomic_write, ApplyPermit, CompleteObservationReceipt, ObservationExpectations, ReleaseIntent,
};

use crate::GraphError;

pub trait ReleaseReceiptWriter {
    fn write(&self, path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> std::io::Result<()>;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter;

impl ReleaseReceiptWriter for AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter {
    fn write(&self, path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        atomic_write(path, content, permit)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ReleaseReceiptStore<W = AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter> {
    path: PathBuf,
    writer: W,
}

impl ReleaseReceiptStore {
    pub fn new(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        Self::with_writer(path, AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter)
    }
}

impl<W: ReleaseReceiptWriter> ReleaseReceiptStore<W> {
    pub fn with_writer(path: impl Into<PathBuf>, writer: W) -> Self {
        Self {
            path: path.into(),
            writer,
        }
    }

    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.path
    }

//! Atomic explicit-path persistence for final observation receipts.
//!
//! Receipts are output evidence, never an input authority. This store exposes
//! no load-as-proof path and accepts only a receipt that revalidates against
//! the exact intent and artifact expectations being converged.

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use callisto_model::{
    atomic::atomic_write, ApplyPermit, CompleteObservationReceipt, ObservationExpectations, ReleaseIntent,
};

use crate::GraphError;

pub trait ReleaseReceiptWriter {
    fn write(&self, path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> std::io::Result<()>;
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter;

impl ReleaseReceiptWriter for AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter {
    fn write(&self, path: &Path, content: &str, permit: &ApplyPermit) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        atomic_write(path, content, permit)
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ReleaseReceiptStore<W = AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter> {
    path: PathBuf,
    writer: W,
}

impl ReleaseReceiptStore {
    pub fn new(path: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
        Self::with_writer(path, AtomicReleaseReceiptWriter)
    }
}

impl<W: ReleaseReceiptWriter> ReleaseReceiptStore<W> {
    pub fn with_writer(path: impl Into<PathBuf>, writer: W) -> Self {
        Self {
            path: path.into(),

        }

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error, Diagnostic)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum CliError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Graph(#[source] Box<GraphError>),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Locate(#[from] LocateError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Config(#[from] ConfigError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Command(#[from] CommandError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(callisto::registry_error),
        help("verify registry credentials/authentication and network connectivity, then retry")
    )]
    Registry(#[from] callisto_model::RegistryError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    ChangesetParse(#[from] callisto_format::ParseError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    ChangesetWrite(#[from] callisto_format::WriteError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Manifest(#[from] callisto_model::ManifestError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    Vcs(#[from] callisto_vcs::VcsError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(transparent)]
    ReleasePrDecision(#[from] callisto_model::ReleasePrDecisionError),

    #[error(transparent)]
    #[diagnostic(code(callisto::pre_json_error))]
    PreJson(#[from] callisto_format::PreJsonError),

    #[error("I/O error{}", match &path {
        Some(p) => format!(" accessing `{}`", p.display()),
        None => String::new(),
    })]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(callisto::io_error),
        help("check that the path exists and that you have permission to access it")
    )]
    Io {
        #[source]
        source: std::io::Error,
        path: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
    },

    #[error("refusing to prompt interactively: stdin is not a terminal and no non-interactive flags were given")]
    #[diagnostic(
        code(callisto::not_a_tty),
        help("specify package names explicitly via `callisto add --package <name>:<severity>` in CI environments")
    )]
    NotATty,

    #[error("{0}")]
    #[diagnostic(code(callisto::error))]
    Other(String),
}

impl From<GraphError> for CliError {
    fn from(error: GraphError) -> Self {
        Self::Graph(Box::new(error))
    }
}

impl From<std::io::Error> for CliError {
    fn from(source: std::io::Error) -> Self {
        CliError::Io { source, path: None }
    }
}
